title: Maximal nonempty closed counterexample to proper algebraization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose completion of coherent modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, pqf-def-coherent] along $I\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is not an equivalence. There exist a closed immersion $j:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with $Z$ nonempty and Noetherian and $f\circ j$ proper, and a coherent formal module $M$ on $(Z,I\mathcal O_Z)$ which is not isomorphic to the completion of any coherent module. Moreover, for every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $K$ of $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], completion on its closed subscheme $V(K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] along the extension of $I\mathcal O_Z$ is an equivalence. This assertion holds for every Noetherian witness on $V(K)$.

proof.text: Properness makes X Noetherian. Identify the kernel ideal of Spec(A/I) with the ideal sheaf of I: compose the map on global sections with the Gamma-Spec isomorphism, apply naturality, ker(A -> A/I)=I, and ideal map/comap along a ring equivalence. Proper full faithfulness and the definition of equivalence imply that failure of equivalence supplies a coherent formal object outside the essential image.

Let S be the set of kernels of closed immersions j:Z -> X with proper composite j followed by f and failing completion on Z. The identity immersion gives a member of S. Apply the ideal-sheaf maximal-element clause of Noetherian ACC, using the coherent first term of the failing formal object as its ambient coherent module argument. Obtain a maximal kernel L and an immersion j realizing it; the proper composite supplies Noetherianity on Z.

If Z were empty, its unique map into projective space of dimension zero would be a closed immersion. Uniqueness of maps from an empty scheme identifies its composite structural map with j followed by f. The projective existence theorem gives an equivalence for precisely the kernel completion ideal, contradicting failure. Apply proper full faithfulness again to obtain M outside the essential image.

For nonzero K on Z, compose its canonical closed immersion with j. The composite kernel contains j.ker. If the kernels were equal, the equal-ideal closed-immersion isomorphism theorem would make K.subschemeι an isomorphism, whose kernel is zero; ker_subschemeι=K contradicts nonzero K. Hence the composite kernel strictly exceeds L. Failure of completion on this quotient would put that larger kernel in S, contradicting maximality. The comap composition formula gives the stated completion ideal. Proof irrelevance identifies all Noetherian witnesses.

mathlib_searches.query: Failure of algebraization of coherent formal modules on a proper scheme reduces to a maximal closed subscheme with every nonzero closed quotient algebraizable
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results: affine transition limits, finite morphisms, integral schemes, and a properness criterion over a field. None gives this algebraization reduction.

Library search found full faithfulness, devissage, projective existence, formal pullback, push-pull and the proved ProjectiveSpace.exists_isClosedImmersion_finite_coordinates. No maximal algebraization counterexample theorem or direct proper-existence proof. The 088E Chow comparison has a different conclusion about proper support, and is not applicable on an already proper scheme.
